Fastbloom Support

Struggling with food, eating or your body? Free help

  • Emergency: call your local emergency number (911 in the US and Canada, 999 in the UK, 112 in the EU, 000 in Australia).
  • US and Canada: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline: call or text 988, 24/7, free and confidential.
  • US: ANAD (National Association of Anorexia Nervosa and Associated Disorders), free eating-disorder support: anad.org.
  • UK: Beat, the UK's eating disorder charity: beateatingdisorders.org.uk.
  • Canada: NEDIC (National Eating Disorder Information Centre): nedic.ca.
  • Australia: Butterfly Foundation: butterfly.org.au.
  • Anywhere else: findahelpline.com lists free, confidential helplines by country.

These resources are always free in Fastbloom and never shown next to ads. Fastbloom is not a crisis or medical service and can't respond to emergencies. Fastbloom is an independent app and is not affiliated with these organizations.

Answers to common questions. Still stuck? Email SUPPORT_EMAIL_TBD and a human will reply, usually within 2 business days.

Fasting and safety

Is Fastbloom medical advice?

No. Fastbloom is a tracking and education tool, not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat or prevent any condition and does not replace your doctor, dietitian or pharmacist. Health information in the app cites its sources with a label showing how strong the evidence is; your own results may differ. Talk to a healthcare professional before fasting, especially if you have a health condition, take medication or are pregnant or breastfeeding.

Why does Fastbloom ask safety questions? Why can't I start a 24-hour fast?

During onboarding you can answer a short, optional safety check: whether you are under 18, pregnant or breastfeeding, have a history of an eating disorder, or take medication for diabetes. Fasting can be risky in these situations, so fasts of 24 hours or longer are offered only to adults who report none of these, and the app shows extra guidance. Your answers stay on your iPhone and are never sent anywhere or given to ad companies. You can review them in Fastbloom Settings.

If you take insulin or other diabetes medication, fasting can cause dangerously low blood sugar. Don't change how you eat or take your medication without talking to your doctor.

How does GLP-1 tracking work?

You can log your medication, dose and injection site, and any side effects, so you have a private record to look back on or show your doctor. Fastbloom does not tell you what dose to take or when, and it does not read or write medications in Apple Health. Always follow your prescriber's instructions and the medication's leaflet.

Using Fastbloom

How do I connect Apple Health? What does Fastbloom read and write?

Turn on Apple Health in Fastbloom Settings and choose what to allow in the iOS screen that appears. Fastbloom can write the weight, water and protein you log, and read weight, water, protein and food energy. Food energy is used only to ask "did you break your fast?" when another app logs food during a fast. Health data stays on your iPhone and is never shared with ad companies or anyone else. To change access later: Settings > Health > Data Access & Devices > Fastbloom.

How is the weekly recap written? Is it sent anywhere?

On iOS 26 or later with Apple Intelligence turned on, the recap is written by Apple's on-device AI model. Otherwise Fastbloom uses a built-in template. Either way it is created on your iPhone and nothing is sent to us or any server. Free users can unlock a recap by choosing to watch a short ad; Pro includes it.

Widgets, Live Activities and Siri

Add a Fastbloom widget from your Home Screen or Lock Screen, and your running fast also appears as a Live Activity on the Lock Screen and Dynamic Island. You can start or end a fast and log water from widgets, Siri or the Shortcuts app. Widgets and Live Activities show your fast to anyone who can see your phone; turn Live Activities off in Settings > Fastbloom if you prefer.

How do fasting buddies work?

Share a buddy code from the app with a friend through Messages or any app in the share sheet. The code holds only the display name you choose, a random code ID, your running fast's start time and goal, and your weekly goal progress. There is no server, so we never see it. To see a friend's progress, import the code they send you; it is saved on your iPhone only.

What notifications does Fastbloom send?

A notification when you reach your fasting goal, eating-window and break-fast reminders if you turn them on, and, if you start a free trial, a reminder 2 days before it ends. They are scheduled on your iPhone, not sent from a server. Turn them off in Settings > Notifications > Fastbloom.

Your data and privacy

Where is my data stored? Can the developer see it?

On your iPhone. There is no account and no server of ours, so we can't see your fasts, weight, notes or GLP-1 logs. Your fasts' times, goal and plan name are also copied to your own iCloud, which we can't access either (see the next answer). Ads in the free version never receive this information or anything from Apple Health. Full details: privacy policy.

I got a new iPhone or reinstalled the app. Will I lose my fast?

No. Fastbloom keeps a small copy of your fasts in your own iCloud (if iCloud is on): the fast you are running now, and each finished fast's start and end time, goal and plan name. After a reinstall, or on a new iPhone signed in to the same Apple ID, they come back automatically. Fasts you deleted stay deleted. This is on by default; you can switch it off in Fastbloom Settings > Export and restore ("Keep fast history in my iCloud"), which removes the finished-fast copy from iCloud. Notes, moods, weight, water, protein, GLP-1 logs and Apple Health data are not in iCloud: they move to a new iPhone with an iCloud Backup, a computer backup or Apple's Quick Start transfer. Weight, water and protein you wrote to Apple Health are also kept in Health.

How do I delete my data?
  • Single entries: delete fasts, notes and logs where they are listed.
  • Everything: use "Delete everything" in Fastbloom Settings and confirm. This erases your data on this iPhone, widget data, and the copy of your fasts (running and finished) in your iCloud. It can't be undone.
  • Deleting the app also removes its data on your iPhone, but not the copy of your fasts in iCloud or a this-iPhone-only Keychain copy of a running fast that iOS may keep (use "Delete everything" first to clear both), not data it wrote to Apple Health (delete that in the Health app), and it does not cancel a subscription.

Purchases and subscriptions

Fastbloom Pro is available as Pro Yearly (US$24.99 per year in the US, with a 7-day free trial for eligible new subscribers) or Pro Lifetime (one payment, US$44.99 in the US). Prices are shown in the app in your currency before you buy.

How do I restore my purchase?
  1. Make sure you are signed in to the App Store with the same Apple ID you used to buy Fastbloom Pro (Settings > [your name] > Media & Purchases).
  2. Open Fastbloom, go to Settings and tap Restore Purchases (it is also on the Pro screen).
  3. If you got Pro through Family Sharing, make sure Purchase Sharing is on for your family group.

Restoring needs an internet connection to reach the App Store. If it says nothing was found, email us with the approximate purchase date (never send card details); we can't see your Apple ID, but we can help you check.

How do I cancel my free trial or subscription?

Subscriptions are managed by Apple. Deleting the app does not cancel a subscription.

  1. Open the iPhone Settings app.
  2. Tap your name, then Subscriptions.
  3. Tap Fastbloom Pro, then Cancel Subscription (or Cancel Free Trial).

Or, inside Fastbloom: Settings > Manage subscription opens the same Apple screen.

To avoid being charged after a free trial, cancel at least 24 hours before the trial ends. The app can send you a reminder 2 days before the trial ends if notifications are on. If you cancel during a trial, Apple may end Pro access right away. If you cancel a paid subscription, you keep Pro until the end of the period you paid for. Apple's guide: Cancel a subscription from Apple.

How do I get a refund?

Apple processes every payment, so refunds come from Apple: go to reportaproblem.apple.com, sign in, choose "Request a refund" and pick the Fastbloom purchase. We can't issue refunds directly, but email us if something went wrong and we'll do what we can.

I have a subscription. Can I switch to Lifetime?

Yes. Buy Lifetime in the app, then cancel the subscription in Settings > [your name] > Subscriptions so it doesn't renew. The app reminds you to do this. Apple decides whether any unused subscription time is refunded.

Why do I see ads, and how do I turn them off?

The free version is funded by ads. Fastbloom Pro (subscription or lifetime) removes all ads. To stop personalized ads without buying anything, choose "Ask App Not to Track" (or change it later in Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking) and review your choices in Fastbloom Settings > Ad Privacy Choices. Details are in the privacy policy.
